note on spurces: everything except aposticha body adapted from sergius by I. Galadza and edited by me
ps140: What now shall І call you, O apostle?* Heaven, for you have proclaimed the glory of God;* radiance, for you illumined the world with light;* cloud which drops divine water as rain;* most divine cup of wisdom,* which pours forth upon us the wine which gladdens hearts.** Pray that our souls be saved.

What now shall І call you, who are pleasing to God?* Golden ark of the covenant, given by Christ;* river which flows forth out of paradise for us;* lamp shining forth a noetic light;* beacon illumining the whole Church;* bread of Life on the divine table;* beaker of spiritual drink.** Pray that our souls be saved.

What now shall we call you, O beholder of God?* Most active servant of the mysteries of Christ;* wise chief-artisan of the noetic tabernacle,* hewing the tablets of grace;* scribe of the new law* which came forth out of Sion, and preached by you.** Pray that our souls be saved.

What now shall we call you, O glorious one?* Strong treasury of heavenly gifts;* renowned physician of bodies and souls;* fellow laborer of Paul,* and his companion in travel,* recounting the acts of the apostles.* Many are the names, O Luke,* which virtue has devised for you.** Pray  that our souls be saved.

What now shall І proclaim you, O divinely eloquent one?* Disciple, for you have announced to us the glad tidings of Christ;* physician, for you heal the passions of the soul;* luminary, shining forth with noetic light;* footing and foundation of the Faith:* for you have written for us the most precious Gospel.** Pray that our souls be saved.

What now shall І call you, O wondrous one?* Honest witness to the teaching of wisdom;* recorder of the acts and teachings of the apostles;* unshakable pillar of piety;* unshakable rampart of the Church.* Many are your names, O Luke,* and greater yet your gifts.** Pray that our souls be saved.

O apostle of Christ,* recorder of divine dogmas,* and foundation of the Church:* with divine proclamations* you have truly healed the hearts  of all those in the gloom of ignorance,* which have entered into the abyss of despair;* and you have saved them* from the tempest of threefold waves,* as a follower and disciple of Paul, the chosen vessel.* Wherefore, we entreat you:* beseech our Saviour and God* on behalf of those who ever faithfully celebrate** your honoured memory.
aposticha: Grace is poured out upon your lips like a tongue of fire;* you received the Word of light, Apostle Luke,* you proclaimed salvation for those who longed to be made children of light;* writing and teaching the holy gospel in the fragrance of truth;* compiling faithfully the deeds and words of Paul, your teacher,* your holy writings are powerful weapons of light;* through them we pierce the darkness of evil:* pray that we may love the light of all,* that delivered from the corruption of death,* we may be granted peace, eternal light and great mercy.

You beheld the fullness of God's mysteries:* your words are a sure fortress of faith,* to you was entrusted the task of writing the word of life for us:* you faithfully obeyed God's inspiration, eye-witness and minister of the incarnate word,* you beheld Him after the resurrection together with Cleopas,* recognizing Him with hearts aflame in the breaking of bread,* pray that He may fill with the sweetness of divine warmth* the souls of all who keep your holy memory.

Rejoice, blameless writer of the Gospel of joy:* you have recorded for us the conception and preaching of the Baptist;* the wondrous annunciation to the Mother of the Lord;* the ineffable incarnation and birth of the Word who came forth from her womb;* His temptations, miracles and parables, His passion, cross and death,* the glory of His risen Body recognized in the breaking of bread,* His glorious ascension and the coming of the Holy Spirit.* As a faithful witness you compiled the Acts of the Apostles.* You were Paul's companion in travel and his greatest consolation,* beholder of divine mysteries and light of the Church:* guard us all, glorious healer.

O all-wise hunter, holy disciple,* husbandman of the Saviour and preacher of His sufferings:* transcending creation with faith and gathering the nations out of deception* and leading them to the good fragrance,* you have attained unto the heavens.* Standing there before the Judge of all,* pray that He deliver us from our iniquities,* and that we be freed from torment** on the Day of Judgment
aposticha_verses: The heavens tell the glory of God,* and the firmament declares the work of His hands.
Their utterance has gone forth into all the earth,* and their word unto the ends of the world.
